photographs.caption: Coincidentally, I took this picture before the trip. It would be the last day I would see the moon for the next 9 nights.
Sign that marks the city limits of Longyearbyen. Beyond this point you are expected to carry a rifle to protect yourself against polar bears. The rule the island, we are the guests.
Svalbard is one of the places with fastest melting ice in the world. The residents organized a climate protest while we were there.
If you have never seen a frozen river before, this is how it looks like.
The biggest, if not only, supermarket in the entire archipelago (Norwegian side). It is very well stocked. Residents would go there to fill water tanks and carry back to their homes.
Getting ready to visit a closed coal mine.
We visited a closed coal mine (3). We had the opportunity to harvest and bring a little bit of coal as souvenirs.

Coal grows in horizontal segments of the rock. In Svalbard, the segments are about 60cm in height. Based on that, geologists can estimate that the archipelago was around the equator for X years, which is how long biomass would have accumulated to form 60cm of coal. Super cool!
Main road of the coal mine. The total extension is over 50km. We walked about 1km during the tour.
Side road inside the mine, with foundational beams holding the mountain.

Guests were invited to crawl through the shafts. These are the 60cm tunnels that coal used to be. To my surprise, the majority of the people didn't want to crawl. We could go about 30m inside the shaft and then crawl back. It was very peaceful and one of the highlights of the trip.

During another day, we had the opportunity to do a snowmobile excursion. It is a very interesting way to visit a mountain valley. It is impossible to walk, use other vehicles, or animals to move around.
Great views, the rivers were melting which made the excursion more challenging. The season was cut short 30 days earlier than the previous year because of snow conditions.
Pasta bolognese during the expedition. There are no amenities in Svalbard (besides the main city), you need to bring everything that the group will need for the day. Bathroom is all around you!
We had the opportunity to walk in sea ice. Our boat moored close to it and we jumped on the ice (guide went first!).
Sea Ice excursion.
At the very end of the sea ice, there was this huge glacier. Incredible.
We also saw some arctic foxes, they are usually around mountains with a lot of birds. Always hunting. Nature never rests.
Another fox trying to get the best of some birds.
Abandoned city of Pyramiden. It is not allowed to disembark there anymore, but it is cool to see it from a distance. It was the largest russian community in Svalbard.
Svalbard reindeer grazing. They have no predators in the island. Polar bears only hunt them in extreme situations.
Also a Svalbard reindeer. There is a strict no intervention rule, so the corpse could not be moved. It probably died 3-5 years ago.
Rock Ptarmigan.
We decided to join an excursion to climb a mountain. We left early in the morning, but it doesn't matter because it would never get dark. This picture shows how steep the climb was.
Trolstein rock, this is the rock that we were climbing towards.
High spirits during the way up.
We made it. We sat down and had lunch at the peak, the weather was great!
At the top of trollstein!
Hug the wall, don't misstep and don't look down!
Trying to climb a little bit higher at the rock. It was quite scary because the floor was snow and it kept falling to the side, making it narrower.
Trollstein mountain
Starting our way down. It was quite narrow to walk at the top.
On the way down of the mountain, we were supposed to crawl under this glacier and leave on the other side, but because of the weather conditions, we had to change our plans and walk around it.
We did a few boat rides where we could see different mountains, sea ice formations, colors of water and the horizon.
Peaceful sea where mountains were reflected on the water.
Beluga whale in nature.
Bird protected colony, boats cannot even pass near it during mating season.
Mountains after rain. Remember, it never gets dark, so it looks like a sunset, but it was just a funny weather.
Bird watching paradise.
Geologists paradise.
It is like the swiss alps, but in islands.
Mountains from a boat.
Snowy mountains.
More mountains and sea ice.
We think that is a seal over the sea ice.
I love this picture a "sunset" with a three mast ship in front of a snowy mountain.
Glacier and misty mountains.
Walrus in front of a glacier. This is one of my favorite pictures of the trip.
First time I saw an walrus, I had to take a lot of pictures.
Walruses swimming together, male and female.
A bearded seal resting on sea ice.
Mother and baby seal resting on ice.
More seals!
Longyearbyen beach
Imagine living here in this cabin. You can see whales from your living room.
Great ski conditions...
I remember freezing and thawing from peak to pit.
On the following days, the conditions improved a lot.
Once we left the padel, the city was covered in snow! Magical weather.
Morretes is a staple visit every time I return to Brazil. I love the food there.
Typical road store in between cities of Brazil. They usually sell artisanal food and crafts. This one was selling corn-based snacks and banana liquors.
A Red-necked Tanager accidentally caught on camera.
Pico do Marumbi. One of the highest peaks in my home state.
Oscar Niemeyer museum.
Traditional restaurant in Brazil. We had "feijoada" a famous dish usually eaten on Saturday.
50% discount for those wearing the official Jersey.
Flamingo with friends.
Took my friend and family to try Indian food for the first time.
At the beach with cousins
Caiobá beach, near my hometown. The day was great!
Maastricht from the top. Ferris wheel picture during a xmas market.
Unbelievable limestone mine in Valkenburg, Netherlands.
Another xmas market in Monschau, Germany. It is a very small city and a picture from this bridge is what every one does.
Cozy streets of Monschau.
Luxemburg city viewpoint.
Main attraction of Luxemburg city.

There's an interesting story behind this picture. During World War II, the Nazis used the former Neumünster Abbey as a prison for resistance fighters and political prisoners. Its high walls prevented people from seeing inside from the streets, but the courtyard was visible from this viewpoint above. Families would gather here to catch a glimpse of their loved ones and discreetly say goodbye, sometimes for the last time, before they were transferred to other prisons or concentration camps.

In the woods near Bastogne, Belgium, you can still see the foxholes dug by American soldiers during the Battle of the Bulge in the winter of 1944–1945. These small holes provided shelter from German artillery fire while soldiers endured freezing temperatures and heavy snow. This is where Easy Company of the 101st Airborne Division, made famous by the HBO series *Band of Brothers*, held its positions for weeks. In January 1945, the company advanced from these woods to attack the nearby village of Foy, a battle depicted in the series. More than 80 years later, many of the original foxholes are still visible among the trees.
Clerics tower with moon.
Igreja do carmo
Tiles of Igreja do Carmo
Soccer match between "Dragoes do Porto" e "Benfica de Lisboa".
Utrecht canals during the Fall.
We started our trip in Trogir, which has a big marina for yacht charting.
The boat in the center would be ours for the next days. It was a Bavaria 42 named Pošip, which is the name of a grape in Croatia.
It looks exactly like other Bavaria's we practiced during our sailing lessons. Galley, living room, and one room at the back.
We anchored in our first night. We had some trouble finding a good spot, but it was part of the adventure. We prayed to Poseidon that night.
Night sky at anchor.
In the following day, we woke up to this view and went for a swim.
Here is a picture of us figuring out anchoring details.
There was a storm forecast, so we radioed and moored at Milna's marina. Unfortunately, the person that hates using the phone is the one with the radio certification.
Pošip when we were moored at the marina in Milna.
See the fish during the day, eat the fish during the night.
On the way back to Trogir, we were racing this other boat. The wind was great!
Beautiful sunset when we were returning the boat.
Shall we go to the beach? Yes, which one? The hardest one!
We hiked and climbed to get to this beach.
It was very worth it. Free, not crowded, and beautiful.
There were also some goats foraging for food.
Once you start using fins, it is hard to stop using them. These long fins are easy to disassemble, so they fit in a backpack and go into the airplane cabin!
Another day, another beach, Cala Petita.
These are the famous Coves del Drach, an unfortunately, private museum, but quite interesting rock formation. The water is crystal clear.
Kayaking in the northern side of Mallorca. It was my 34th birthday on this day.
How many feet do you have!? 𓆨
Walking would have been faster...
Prince Hendrik's hunting room Paleis Het Loo is filled with unusual trophies, including a bearskin rug, an alligator, and an elephant's foot used as a wastebasket. So sad to see.
First time visiting the historical windmills at Kinderdijk! Really nice place.
Valk sailboat, 22 feet, no interior cabin, only main sail.
Day at the lake practicing some sailing
Early morning with fresh snow. Great day in the mountain.
Sausage party!
The 1991 World Cup Slalom piste
South park characters
Skiing with friends is always better!
Slava Ukraine!
Dune Imperium: Uprising, quickly became my favorite board game.
Simple visit to meet great friends.
Ćevapi, hvala!
Visiting Victoria's Memorial with our great friend S.B.
Lush Kolkata
Indian museum of archeology
Victoria's Memorial, beautiful building, but memories from a dark past in India's history.
Painting inside Victoria's memorial.
Boat trip at the Hooghly river.
I think it was the place that I sweat the most in my life. Luckily, the coconut water is delicious.

We were visiting in a very special occasion: durga puja. In this picture, we were visiting a street pandal, which are massive constructions built only for this celebration. We can see the hindu goddess Durga defeating the demon Mahishasura, often surrounded by her children: Lakshmi, Saraswati, Ganesha, and Kartikeya.
Durga defeating Mahishasura

Interesting street in Kolkata where all the stands sell educational book, for all known exams, engineering, medicine, law, literature. If you can't find something that you are looking for, people from nearby stands will come and help you with their friends, very nice atmosphere.
How the streets look like during the Durga Puja celebration.

Our friend welcomed us into their family home, where we had the chance to meet their relatives and share a homemade Indian lunch. A lovely experience of local hospitality, with delicious food and a warm, welcoming atmosphere.
Such a lovely family. One of the best cultural experiences I have ever had.

Streets of green Kalyani, we drew a lot of eyes on the streets. First time I was asked to take a picture with someone I never met before. I gladly accepted, but regret not taking one myself with my phone.
Pandals are also built in smaller cities, they are even more impressive than the ones in big cities.
Pandal made of sea shells. I can't believe they tear it down and rebuild something different each year.
Street food during durga puja celebration.
Taj Mahal is a world wonder everyone should visit once.
The classical picture from Taj. I love how the majority of the visitors were from India and not from abroad. This is not the common case in Europe.
Different angle from Taj Mahal
Taj Mahaltje. The built a smaller one across the river...
Red castle in New Delhi, another incredible place that we learnt about the resistance movements leading to India's independence.
Traditional fondue restaurant in Annecy
Annecy castle in the city canals, it is even prettier during the evening!
Lac du annecy, a lot of sailing and motor boats. The day was great for sailing.
Traditional hotel in Chamonix. You can see the fastest shrinking glacier of Europe in the top right corner.
One of the seven lakes in the hike near Zermatt
View o Lauterbrunnen valley from Winteregg.
View from Mannlichen
Matterhorn showing its face at the end of the hike! Most of the day it was fully covered in clouds.
Mirror lake near Matterhorn. The red flowers at the background gave such a nice contrast.
Glacier lake with Matterhorn at the end.
Hike near Zermatt. There used to be a glacier on the right side of this hill.

A traditional swiss potato dish in the middle of a hike. I almost couldn't believe when I saw it. Imagine hiking for 20km and assuming you only have protein bars to eat and then you find this in the middle of nowhere!
The best picture of Matterhorn from this trip.
Lauterbrunnen waterfall
Cows in lauterbrunnen valley
Cows in lauterbrunnen valley.
Lauterbrunnen valley
View of Lauterbrunnen valley from Mannlichen. Can you spot Rivendell at the end?
Glacier canyon
Old glacier corridor. The glacier melted in recent years and a 300 meter catwalk was constructed. Incredible to imagine this entire volume was covered in ice.
Great trip with a great partner. Love you.

Café Piolho, a traditional student café in Porto, opened in 1909. Its nickname means "louse", supposedly because so many students crowded inside. During Portugal's dictatorship (1933–1974), it became a meeting place for political resistance. According to local legend, customers would scratch their heads to warn others when the secret police entered, another possible explanation for its unusual nickname.
"Camels' drool", horrible name, great flavor. I recommend you to try it.
Master and Commander, F.A
Traditional dutch shallow boat. The lateral "wings" serve as retractable keels.
Different colors every time you go.
Our group for this weekend
After all these years, this is still the best pizza I have ever had. Juliana's pizzaria, near Brooklyn Bridge Park.

photographs.caption: Enjoying the sunset from a desert dune. The sand behaves like water, sliding down on itself.
Old town of Fez seen from a nearby hill. The green roof is the mosque and university of al-Qarawiyyin.

The traditional tanneries of Fez are famous for their centuries-old leather-making techniques, but the work is extremely demanding, with workers exposed to harsh chemicals, strong odors, and difficult physical conditions.
The old medina of Morocco are usually full of street animals. Being a cat lover, it was always hard to see kittens struggling for food and surviving the pedestrian traffic.
A chicken butcher in the old medina. Meat is sold very fresh here.

Traditional Moroccan riads were built around beautiful interior courtyards, where extended families could live together across several generations. Nowadays, most of them were converted into hotels with multiple guest rooms.
Cemetery across the hills outside the old medina of Fez. Thousands of simple white gravestones cover the landscape, reflecting the Islamic tradition of modest burials.
In our way to the desert, we slept in a guest house decorated with traditional Berber objects.
We have reached Merzouga. The desert that we would spend the next two nights.
Berber, ethnic group indigenous to North Africa, settlement. The following pictures show how their settlement is organized.
There is a communal kitchen and when the fireplace is lit, all the meals are cooked together.
Common room in one of the tents. Place where people use a storage and spent time socializing or working.
Another tent is used as bedroom. No mattresses, but a lot of blanked and carpets. It gets really cold very fast.
Desert settlement of Khamlia.
Our desert guide, taught us a lot. Feel the warm wind!

We listened to traditional Gnawa music, a unique blend of African rhythms, spiritual chants, and Moroccan influences. The Gnawa are a cultural and musical community in Morocco, descended in part from enslaved people brought from sub-Saharan Africa, particularly the Sahel region. Their music preserves elements of their West African heritage and has become an important part of Moroccan culture.
Night at the desert, dinner, cold winds, cold sand, but starry skies.
Another desert guide. He taught me how to do the cheche headwrap.
View from our tent. Fun fact, if you shower once the sun is set, the water will be very very cold. Am I really complaining about water temperature in a desert???
Oasis and settlements seen from above. Outside this strip of green, everything else is sand and rocks.
Inside an Oasis. It serves as a communal fertile land for nearby settlements. We could smell all sorts of herbs, spices, and date trees.
City of Ait Benhaddou. A lot of movies were recorder here, including Gladiator and the famous brazilian soap opera: "O Clone".
MF and Ait Benhaddou in the background.
Hiking through a canyon.
Ait Benhaddou from the top.

Unfortunately, what initially seemed like a genuinely friendly encounter turned into an uncomfortable experience when the lady became quite insistent on being paid for the photograph. It was disappointing to realize that her warmth may have been more transactional than it first appeared.
Traditional lamp store in Marrakesh.

The Saadian Tombs in Marrakech, the final resting place of members of the Saadian dynasty, dating back to the 16th century. The royal tombs are surrounded by beautifully decorated marble columns and colorful mosaics.
The intricate architecture of the Saadian Tombs, featuring elaborate carved stucco, ornate arches, and richly decorated cedarwood ceilings. A beautiful example of traditional Moroccan craftsmanship.
We did crash course on Arabic calligraphy. It was an amazing experience, but it takes a lifetime to master.
Zila, the cat in the riad that we were staying.
Private gardens from Yves Saint Laurent.

Traditional Dutch wooden clogs are made using copying machines. A wooden block is carved into a shoe by a rotating blade that follows the shape of a model clog, much like a key-cutting machine. A second machine hollows out the inside, producing a nearly finished clog in minutes!

Prague’s Astronomical Clock, built in 1410, is the oldest astronomical clock still operating in the world. Besides telling time, it tracks the positions of the Sun and Moon, shows the phases of the Moon, and features a parade of the Twelve Apostles every hour. Over 600 years of engineering!
Charles bridge built in 1357.
Prague is a charming city that looks very medieval. Great place to visit during the winter.
Award winning sweet display from a confectionery in Prague. The popcorn one was delicious (it is a cake).
Bled lake and Blejski castle. I don't recommend the "Bled cake" invented by a hotel nearby the lake.
A glimpse of what Slovenia's capital looks like.
War cemetery of Austro-Hungarian soldiers who died between 1915 and 1917 while fighting on the nearby Krn mountain front, between Austria-Hungary and Italy.
Apres drinks with friends.
Almost too hot to ski!
We unfortunately good unlucky with the weather. It was raining the entire night and the market was very crowded. Fun day with friends though.
All the bones are real, the cemetery was overcrowded and decided to use the bones as decoration for the chapel. It from about 5.000 people. Such a cool place!
Small roman temple in the city of Évora.
Bolsa's palace in the city of Porto. I highly recommend the guided visit inside. There is a very special room at the end.
Blue painted tiles at the train station in Porto.
Gold coated church in Porto. All the gold came from Brasil, of course.
Ribeirinha river during night, after a dinner with friends and family.
Coimbra University. It is one of the oldest universities in Europe. Dates from the period of world exploration when they discovered the "new continent".
Nazaré beaches. It is the place of one of the most famous surf competitions.
Rock bottom.
Quinta da Regaleira on a fog day.
The colorful Palácio da Pena in Sintra, Portugal, was built in the 19th century by King Ferdinand II on the ruins of an old monastery.
Mont Serrate palace. Inside you can see Arabic architecture influence and how good was life for the family living there.
De devil's throat near Lisbon.
Sea food platter to share. I ate most of it.
Beautiful sweet display in Lison, my favorite one is not in the picture, "travesseiro da piriquita".
Commerce Square in Lisbon.
Mosteiro dos Jeronimos. Fun fact: Pero Vaz de Caminha was buried in a nearby church.
Dutch parliament building and Mauritshaus. We also visited the Escher museum this day.
De Haar castle gardens with family.
Fireplace inside the castle.
More friends are joining!
We never played this game again.
Visiting a coal mine near Essen was one of the highlights of the trip!
Very hard conditions for workers, it was almost guaranteed that you would become deaf working here.
Fascinating machinery
Pampus island from the boat
Shared cabin during sailing lesson.
Second weekend of sailing lessons, the weather was much more forgiving and we learnt and enjoyed so much more.
Freediving lesson seen from above. A group of 3 students spread in a ring formation of buoys.
Getting ready before swimming 200m towards the buoy setup.
During this trip I learnt that I'm terrible at "ear equalization", so free diving is very hard for me.
Fun in the water, except for the cold. It was so cold!
All the free divers from underwater. Some people were going deeper than 85 meters!
Rest day in a nearby beach.
Our cabin during the training.
Miniature Amsterdam!
Glyptotek, incredible museum of statues, plants, and architecture.
We were all beaten by the weather. One of the longest weekends of my life.
The beautiful marina of Den Oever. From this picture you can't imagine the horrible weather we got to get here.
Como lake from Como city
Cozy villages around lake como
Main residence at Villa Melzi
Lake view from Villa Carlotta
Villa Balbianello
Villa Balbianello
View from Belaggio
Villa from the city of Varenna
We had great days for skiing and everyone learned and improved so much. Great winter days.
Enjoying our time together in the mountains.
We took the opportunity to visit Turin's royal palace. Definitely recommend! Look at this green marble!
Dining hall at turin's royal palace.
Duomo di milano, always impressive, doesn't matter how many times you see it.
The three peaks of Senja. Looks like a sunset, but this was around noon. We had about 2 more hours of daylight left.
Fjordgarden is such a special place, the fog just made it more special.
The only grocery store in town!
Peak a boo.
We saw the northern lights for the first time!
During this moment, it was very strong and impressive, but not always!
That's how you ski in the Netherlands.
Water mirror of Kasteel de Haar.
Panoramic view from sugar loaf, Rio de Janeiro.
I'm watching over Christ from above.
View from Leme, Rio de Janeiro. I love that you can see the top of state on the right side of this picture, among the clouds.
Christ statue floating in the clouds, Leme, Rio de Janeiro.
Historical building in Rio de Janeiro downtown.
Historical building from polish immigrants in a public park in my hometown.
Soccer match from my hometown team.
Lake view from Tapes, RS.
Marina for lake boats in Tapes, RS.
It was such a special event to go for the first time and right after the pandemic. Everyone wearing masks, but at least not as crowded as the future years.
Never played Hippocrates again.
Such a horrible day for a bike ride, but unfortunately, we can't change competition day.
Phew, I was glad when it ended.
Kasteel de haar seen from above!
Such a cool vehicle! Just like MS flight simulator
Man made Rhine canal connecting shipping containers from the North Sea all the way to the Rhine river, which extends all the way to Basel, Switzerland.
Utrecht central station seen from above.
It is a lot of work, but so worth it!
Summer days that we remember during the winter.
We started the trip in London.
London castle
View from St. James Park in London.
We visited the city of Dundee, which is a fond place of ours. This is the main viewpoint of the city.
We started our hikes at a Reindeer conservation near Cairngorms national park.
Small hike at Cairngorms, around a mirrored lake in a bog.
I almost couldn't believe it either, but this is in Scotland. The water was very cold but there were some people swimming.

Salmon climbing the Rogie waterfall for its reproductive life cycle. The jump looks impossible, but you know, nature finds a way. I came with zero expectation of seeing a salmon, but when I saw them it was magical. I think we spent almost one hours watching them jump!
Just an untitled mountain.
The day Marilia ate fish. Up to this day, she says this is the best fish she ever ate.
Picnic table in a rare sunny day.
Old man of storr, such a nice hike. It is one of the few places that that wind is stronger than the Netherlands.
G.O.A.T at old man of Storr
Fairy glen at the island is Skye.
Macro shot of a purple foxglove flower covered in dew.
Quairang hike. I recommend going on a sunny day. The fog and rain only got worse after this picture, it was quite an adventure that we will never forget.
View from the end of the Quairang hike.
Common landscape in the Scottish highlands.
Full of energy and ready to conquer Glen coe!
Glen coe in a rare sunny day.
Resting at the top of a rock.

The lost valley. It can easily be found by following the only trail from the road towards glen coe. Story goes that Clan MacDonald historically used this secret valley to hide cattle they rustled from neighboring clans. I can't imagine doing this hike with cattles....
Glennfinning train bridge, where scenes from Harry Potter were filmed. Quite a crowd was gathered to take this picture!
Crossing the river using three wire bridge. We were going towards a valley with a waterfall at the end.
Such a nice waterfall view to make the hike effort worth it.

Eilean Donan Castle, it is privately owned. It was built on top of this small island with some natural protection from the tides. The moat was like this in the beginning of the visit and almost completely dry at the end.
Oban, a quite and little city in Scotland that I would never want to live.
View of Stirling, where the battle of Stirling bridge happened. William Wallace and Andrew Moray used terrain and a classic bottleneck trap to defeat a larger English army, back in 1297!
I remember listening to Red Hot Chili Pepper since I was in high school, seeing them play live was a night to remember!
Medieval city in the heart of the Netherlands.
Maldives is truly a spectacular place. This is the pier of the island that we were staying.
We have the opportunity to search for whale shark and then swim besides it. One of the best experiences of my life.
We were swimming among a group of nurse sharks.
Here a picture from the boat. It was funny when we reached the place and were instructed to jump in the sea, all we could see was sharks in the water below us.
Sitting on water.
The blue was unbelievable.
10 year anniversary dinner celebration.
Swimming with sea turtles.
Sunset from our island.
Starry night at Maldives.
Tulip fields in the Netherlands
Tulips as far as the eyes can see.
Visiting Keukenhof with friends!
Trying to spot deers at Veluwe National park (We didn't).
I always visit this city when I travel to Brasil. It is a city in between my hometown and the beach. They serve a traditional food called "Barreado"
Rock formation in the shape of a "glass" caused by wind erosion.
Zip lining over a cenote with my grandmother.
Beach trip with old university friends
Versailles garden during the summer is something else! First time visiting with great weather.
Beautiful garden in Versailes
Eating my favorite dish, beef bourguignon, in Paris. It incentivized me to create a "meat with gravy" photo album.
Bridge over river Rhone. Syrah grape plantation at the background. We bought a few bottles to bring home!
We stopped at Cascades du Sautadet for a quick swim in the cold river. It was a great summer day!

Legend says that in 1177, a shepherd was divinely inspired to build Avignon’s famous bridge. Originally 900 metres long with 22 arches, it was repeatedly destroyed by floods from the Rhône River. Abandoned in the 17th century, only four arches survive today.

The Palace of the Popes in Avignon, France. For nearly 70 years, popes ruled the Catholic Church from here instead of Rome. In 1378, a dispute led to two rival popes, one in Rome and another in Avignon, dividing Europe for nearly 40 years. At one point, there were even three! The Italian pope prevailed!
Trebuchet and catapults at les Baux-de-Provence. Incredible visit if you are passing by!
City center of aix-en-provance.
Calanque national park is in my opinion one of the most beautiful parks in Europe. We were so lucky with the weather.
Hiking in Calanque National park. I think we walked around 20km this day.
Grape plantation near aix-en-provance. We were very lucky with the sunset this day.
Kayaking through Gorges du Verdon. The water was incredibly cold, it was impossible to swim, even on a very hot summer day.
Villa Bailieu, a private winery in the heart of provance. Incridible place to visit!
Quick stop at Disney World Paris on the way back home.
Beautiful sunset by the sea during pandemic years.
From the dunes to the sea. It was the best place to go during pandemic.
The day we saw a fox in Zuid Kennermeland dunes!
Discovering the beauty of Zuid Kennermeland dune park. Crystal clear water, we didn't swim this day because it was still very cold, but we definitely returned later during summer.
Beautiful walking route near Voorthuizen. Exactly what we needed during the pandemic!
The day the canals froze and we rushed to Zaanse Schaans to visit the village and enjoy the cold weather! It was such a memorable day.
The dunes in the Netherlands look like the bottom of the sea, transformed by years of plant growth.
Beach and dunes day out. People were enjoying outdoor as much as possible during the pandemic.
Bouillon, a lovely city in Belgium.
Chateau du Facon, great prices when hotels were trying to survive the pandemic!
8km race in The Hague. The last trip before COVID-19 pandemic. If only we knew...
60km Bike ride for a competition
The famous Wellington steak
Heart of Clojure, before LLM's ruined the whole thing.
Under the waterfall
